item.title: Medical association asks for exemption of foreign doctors from the new 400 fee
item.description: The Malta Medical Association is calling on the government to exempt doctors and other essential health workers from the new 400 infrastructure contribution charged when work permits are renewed, and to review the Budget 2027 measures affecting third-country nationals. President Dr Patrick Sammut said Malta cannot depend on foreign professionals while making it harder for them to build a life here, and warned the health sector is already under pressure from population growth, an ageing population and rising demand for medical services. The association said Malta must not rely solely on the training of foreign workers to staff its health service, and issued the statement on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:

President Dr Patrick Sammut said Malta cannot depend on foreign professionals while making it harder for them to build a life here, and warned the health sector is already under pressure from population growth, an ageing population and rising demand for medical services. The association said Malta must not rely solely on the training of foreign workers to staff its health service, and issued the statement on Saturday.

Sources: Newsbook

item.title: Callus: Budget worker measures are a gift to employers exploiting foreign workers
item.description: Moviment Graffitti activist Andre Callus said the Budget 2027 measures targeting third-country nationals were a gift for anyone who wants to exploit those workers in Malta. Speaking on Andrew Azzopardis Saturday programme on Campus 103.7, Callus said affected workers lose access to free childcare and public transport and face an annual 996 charge to drive private vehicles and a 400 infrastructure fee when renewing work permits. He argued the measures make an already vulnerable group more dependent on their employers, and that they target low-paid workers who cannot vote and are disproportionately affected by workplace injuries and deaths.

item.title: ADPD accuses government of pandering to racist sentiment over Budget 2027 worker measures
item.description: ADPD-The Green Party accused the government of putting votes before human dignity through its Budget 2027 measures on third-country nationals. Speaking at a press conference in Valletta on Saturday, party chairperson Sandra Gauci said the governments concept of social justice depends on whether people have a vote, adding that the government was exploiting workers who cannot vote to finance its electoral promises. The party said the budget offers immediate relief while leaving structural problems the economic model, traffic and the sustainability of public finances unaddressed, shifting costs onto future generations facing national debt above 13 billion. The measures will see non-EU workers without long-term residency facing higher work-permit fees and an annual 400 infrastructure contribution.

item.title: Waterspout filmed over the sea off Gozo as storms forecast
item.description: Video filmed on Facebook shows a waterspout over the sea a short distance off the island of Gozo, catching Maltese islands in the early hours of Saturday. The weather is expected to be characterised by thunderstorms, with hail and some heavy showers reaching the southern islands, and the same downpour is forecast for Sunday. Tuesday is expected to be the first day without rain, with showers returning on Thursday.

item.title: Mqabba quarry transformed into 7,000-square-metre Park tal-Mitħna
item.description: Park tal-Mitħna, a 7,000-square-metre public park with a dedicated dog area, was inaugurated on Saturday on a site in Mqabba on the border with Qrendi that had served as a quarry for many years. item.title: Two injured after car overturns and catches fire in Attard
item.description: A 27-year-old driver from al Qormi suffered grievous injuries and an 18-year-old passenger from Swieqi slight injuries after the car they were in struck a lamppost, overturned and caught fire at around 5am on Saturday on Mdina Road in Attard. Both managed to escape the Toyota Vitz before it ignited and were taken to Mater Dei Hospital by ambulance. Police said they were called to the area at about 5am, close to the roundabout near Monte Karmeli and a petrol station forecourt, and are investigating further, with Civil Protection Department firefighters also assisting at the scene.

item.title: Ramla Bay Resort to give TCN workers €400 permit-renewal contribution
item.description: Ramla Bay Resort in Mellieħa has announced a contribution of up to €400 for each of its third-country national workers when their work permits are renewed, to help cover the extra costs of this year's Budget measures. The resort is also launching a company-wide service bonus and a new employee social and wellbeing fund fully funded by the company. It said it will support training for colleagues attending Maltese language courses and taking part in the I Belong programme, aimed at helping them integrate further into Maltese society.

item.title: Cleaner avoids jail for theft after original prison sentence quashed
item.description: A cleaner who was sentenced to three years in prison for stealing jewellery from two homes has been conditionally discharged after her original sentence was quashed. Magistrate Astrid May Grima said Seliam Ann Elbueshi Perry, 46, had served enough time since the offences, had stable employment and had returned some of the stolen jewellery. The case dates back to 2018, with thefts from flats in Sliema and Msida between 2017 and 2018, for which she pleaded guilty in December 2018.

item.title: Cleaner avoids jail for jewellery theft after original sentence quashed

item.title: 21-year-old Mater Dei clerk charged with four terrorism-related offences
item.description: Daniel Spiteri, 21, from abbar, a clerk in the emergency department at Mater Dei Hospital, was charged with four terrorism-related offences and pleaded not guilty before the Court of Magistrates. The counts relate to terrorist recruitment, training, travel and the dissemination of material intended to encourage terrorist activities. Police said the counterterrorism unit opened an inquiry in May 2026 after receiving confidential information about a Maltese national allegedly travelling to Syria in connection with terrorist activities; a search warrant was obtained on 23 October and Spiteri was arrested shortly before 5am on 27 October. No bail application was made at the sitting, with the prosecution conducted by Attorney General lawyers Dejan Darmanin and Mauro Abela and the defence by Ismael Psaila and Amadeus Cachia.

item.title: Credit agency holds Malta's A2 rating but warns on spending and rule of law
item.description: Credit rating agency Moody's affirmed Malta's A2 rating with a stable outlook, but warned that continued government spending and institutional shortcomings are holding back an otherwise resilient economy. The agency expects the fiscal deficit to widen from 2.1% of GDP in 2025 to 2.8% in 2026 before easing to 2.7% in 2027, citing energy subsidies costing around €400 million, higher social security spending and growing public investment. It again flagged rule of law, corruption and money laundering supervision concerns, while noting that Budget 2027's higher tourist contributions and work permit fees could partly offset the additional spending.

item.title: BOV chair says employers should shoulder the cost of TCN budget measures
item.description: Bank of Valletta board chairperson Gordon Cordina said employers should bear the cost of the Budget 2027 measures affecting third-country nationals without long-term residency. Speaking on Campus 103.7 on Saturday, Cordina argued Malta needs an enterprising economy able to sustain the cost of attracting skilled, quality workers rather than one built on low cost. He said the expense would be carried by the sector that benefits most from those workers, and would if necessary be passed on to end consumers, adding that Malta should have moved away from low-cost business models decades ago.

item.title: Saint James performs first specialised heart procedures in private healthcare
item.description: Three specialised heart procedures previously available only through Maltas public health service have been carried out at Saint James Hospital in ejtun, the first such interventions in the countrys private healthcare sector. The work took place in the hospitals new 2.5 million Prof. Albert Fenech Cardiac Suite and included a coronary angiogram and a patent foramen ovale closure, a procedure that seals a small opening between the hearts two upper chambers.

item.title: Two injured after car overturns at Ħ'Attard roundabout
item.description: Two people were taken to Mater Dei Hospital after a serious accident at the roundabout near Monte Karmeli in Ħ'Attard, where a car overturned onto its side. Police said the incident happened at about 5am near a petrol station forecourt, when the driver, a 27-year-old man from Ħal Qormi, lost control of the vehicle; an 18-year-old passenger from Swieqi was also in the car. The driver suffered serious injuries and the passenger lighter ones, and police investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Emeritus judge finds no basis for University probe into statistician Vince Marmarà
item.description: Statistician Vince Marmarà published the full conclusions of a report by retired judge Geoffrey Valenzia, who found no factual basis to justify a University of Malta investigation into alleged professional ethics breaches. Valenzia said the accusations levelled against Marmarà by Arnold Cassola were not supported by facts or evidence, and criticised them as serious and offensive personal allegations. Marmarà said he was making the conclusions public after the competent authorities confirmed that no laws had been breached in the professional work carried out by his company.

item.title: Malta and Turkey discuss closer cooperation on healthcare
item.description: Health Minister Ian Borg held talks with his Turkish counterpart Kemal Memiolu in Istanbul on closer cooperation in digital health, medical innovation and hospital infrastructure. The meetings took place on the sidelines of the 12th Turkish Medical World Congress and follow a two-day visit to Malta last week by a Turkish delegation led by Deputy Health Minister uayip Birinci, which toured Gozo General Hospital.

item.title: Caritas warns Budget measures on migrants risk fuelling discrimination
item.description: Caritas Malta welcomed Budget 2027's social measures, including higher pensions and the minimum wage, extra support for people with disabilities and families in need, and government coverage of social security contributions for young people in long-term rehabilitation. The charity warned that the new fees targeting third-country nationals risk creating a divide between people seen as entitled to social protection and migrant workers treated primarily as economic units. Under the budget, workers without long-term residency lose free childcare and public transport, face a €996 annual charge to drive and a €400 infrastructure contribution fee, and pay higher work permit fees, though nurses and carers are exempt from the permit fee increase.

item.title: Court orders immediate release of tourist jailed over airport bomb remark
item.description: Magistrate Marse-Ann Farrugia ordered the immediate release of Croatian national Blazenko Djuran, 61, after finding that his continued detention was unlawful, upholding a habeas corpus application on his behalf. The court found that a language misunderstanding over the English word "charges" had resulted in his guilty plea being recorded as not guilty, when he had always insisted on his guilt. Djuran had been remanded since 23 October after a sarcastic remark to Ryanair staff at Malta International Airport that his hand luggage was not as though it contained a bomb. The detention was declared unlawful under Article 412B of the Criminal Code.

item.title: Momentum publishes the 22-question survey commissioned for the Yorgen Fenech case
item.description: Momentum published on Saturday the 22-question draft questionnaire run by pollster Vincent Marmars company, Sagalytics, which was commissioned by Raymond Fenech, uncle of businessman Yorgen Fenech. The party also published an extract from the terms of engagement with the polling company.

item.title: Għarb nursing home on agricultural land set for approval after 850 objections
item.description: A nursing home planned on agricultural land in Għarb is expected to be approved on 10 November after a fourth attempt, having attracted more than 850 objections. The Environment and Resources Authority deemed the application acceptable after the plans were cut from 68 to 32 beds, for a total of 48, down from the 94 proposed in 2022, though it said any intervention beyond the development zone remained unacceptable. The land, owned by Emanuel Joseph Farrugia, lies outside the development zone, and the case is due to be decided by the Planning Commission.

item.title: Qrendi residents gatecrash garden inauguration over major development
item.description: Residents and activists gatecrashed the inauguration of a new garden in Qrendi to confront Environment Minister Miriam Dalli over a proposed major residential development in the village. The dispute centres on planning application PC/00053/26, which proposes residential buildings reaching 17.5 metres high on vacant land off Triq Dun Nerik Mahoney and Triq San Nikola, close to a historic tower. Protesters said the community had lost confidence in the planning process.
